items.title: 68004_Howard McGhee oral history interview
items.q: Since he was working for me, he got me a gig in St. Louis with Billie. We played a dance there, and then we played one in Chicago and played one in Milwaukee, and one in Gary, Indiana.

ctx.x: and fix breakfast for me and my old lady and everything. The Lady was somethin' else.

At one time I had a manager named Jud Bernard, and he liked Lady; you know, he thought the world of her. So he booked me on a big with her... Since he was working for me, he got me a gig in St. Louis with Billie. We played a dance there, and then we played one in Chicago and played one in Milwaukee, and one in Gary, Indiana. That's how I really got tight with Lady, and I realized how much talent she really had. Because she really did draw the people in, and the people just loved her -- and I loved her too. And…

But man, she was something else. Boy... After I got off to lead this date, because I had a sextet and she had a rhythm section, you know... So I'd do my bit, and then I'd get off and then she'd come on. And man, I used to stand right there in the wing and just listen to her sing, and say, "God be damned, boy, if I could sing like that I'd be somebody."
